==English==

===Etymology===
{{calque|en|fr|racine caractéristique}}, the term preferred by French mathematician {{w|Augustin-Louis Cauchy}} (1789–1857).

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|linear algebra}} An [[eigenvalue]].

Fuller, ''Basic Matrix Theory'', 2017, Dover, [https://books.google.com.au/books?id=Yl4nDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA217&dq=%22characteristic+root%22%7C%22characteristic+roots%22&hl=en&sa=X&ved=0ahUKEwjEj9HW8JLYAhVrxYMKHQlRCI8Q6AEIigIwKg#v=onepage&q=%22characteristic%20root%22%7C%22characteristic%20roots%22&f=false page 217],
#*: There is an important relationship between the '''characteristic roots''' of a symmetric matrix and the ''r'' and ''p'' of the associated quadratic form. It is true that the number of positive '''characteristic roots''' is ''p'', whereas the number of nonzero '''characteristic roots''' is ''r''.

|passage=The determinant of a matrix is the product of its '''characteristic roots'''.}}
